chapter.title: Interrupts
chapter.para: A guest gets the interrupts of the devices that the hypervisor emulates for it; the hypervisor does not pass the interrupts of the host to a guest, except as this chapter says.

section.para: On x86_64 the hypervisor shall emulate for each VM a pair of 8259A interrupt controllers, programmed by the guest through their ports (initialization and operation command words, interrupt masks, priorities, end of interrupt, cascade through IRQ 2, reading of the request and service registers).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: JetOS for x86_64 drives the 8259A pair.

formalpara.title: Traceability

section.para: On x86_64 the hypervisor shall reset the emulated 8259A pair of a VM when it loads the VM.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Each start of a guest finds its interrupt controllers as at power-on.

section.para: On x86_64 the hypervisor shall deliver an interrupt of the emulated controller to the guest when the guest can take it, that is when its interrupt flag is set and it is not in the shadow of an instruction.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: An interrupt must not interrupt what the guest does not allow.

section.para: On x86_64 the hypervisor shall let a guest that has halted with interrupts enabled wait for an interrupt.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A guest halts to wait for its next interrupt.

section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall emulate for each VM the distributor of a GICv2 for the interrupts 0 to 31 and one CPU.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: JetOS for arm64 drives a GICv2, and needs the interrupt of its timer.

formalpara.title: Traceability

section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall give the guest the CPU interface of the host through the virtual CPU interface of the processor.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: JetOS for arm64 drives a GICv2, and needs the interrupt of its timer.

formalpara.title: Traceability
formalpara.para: HLR_STAGE2_STAGE2_BUILD_02 HLR_GIC_GIC_READ32_01 HLR_GIC_GIC_WRITE32_01 HLR_GIC_GIC_WRITE8_01 HLR_GIC_GIC_GICV_BASE_01 HLR_GIC_GIC_INIT_CPU_02 HLR_GIC_GIC_VCPU_RESET_01

section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall give the guest the interrupt of its virtual timer when the guest's distributor is on and the interrupt is enabled in it, with the priority that the guest gave it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The guest must see the tick as its own, once.

section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall take back the interrupt of the virtual timer from the guest if the guest disables it before it was taken.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A guest must not take an interrupt that it has disabled.

section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall deliver each interrupt of the virtual timer to the guest once.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The guest must see the tick as its own, once.

section.para: The hypervisor shall use, for itself, only the interrupts of the host that it needs: on x86_64 the local APIC timer, on arm64 the virtual timer and the maintenance interrupt of the GIC.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The hypervisor must not be disturbed by what it did not ask for.

section.para: The hypervisor shall ignore a spurious interrupt, and report any other interrupt that it does not use on its console and go on.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The hypervisor must not be disturbed by what it did not ask for.

section.para: The hypervisor shall treat an exception of its own as a fatal error.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: An exception in the hypervisor means that it can no longer guarantee the isolation of the VMs.
